title: AI papers (weekly): 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-26
global_caveat: This is an inferred ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart; citation evidence is limited for these very recent papers.

sections.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
sections.abstract: The paper combines recurrent Mamba state, local attention, and persistent content memory for long-horizon controllable humanoid motion, reporting 39.52-second rollouts and lower inference latency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce persistent content memory and an execution path tailored to the Mamba-based diffusion model; the arXiv paper reports a 6.138× median paired speedup on an RTX 4090 while preserving tested outputs and states.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the framework addresses controllable humanoid motion but not object manipulation; they identify whole-body loco-manipulation as future work.
sections.evidence: Collector score 18.355; Hugging Face paper card recorded 224 upvotes and 40 GitHub stars; one cross-list.

sections.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
sections.abstract: WorldLeague evaluates progress toward physical goals across 60 simulated robot tasks and six capability dimensions, reporting both interactive progress and task success.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a shared Physical Agency Profile that distinguishes physical progress from answering questions about an episode; in their evaluation of 13 systems, 71.8% of episodes with full terminal-QA credit received zero operation credit.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison covers 60 simulated tasks and 13 representative systems; it does not establish how the profile transfers to physical robot deployments.
sections.evidence: Collector score 16.328; Hugging Face paper card recorded 137 upvotes and 21 GitHub stars.

sections.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
sections.abstract: Embo-Harness studies prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use in robotic harnesses that use frontier multimodal models directly as closed-loop policies.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors distill six harness-design findings and report an 83.3% RoboLab-120 success rate, 26.2 percentage points above their strongest reported baseline, plus success in 15 of 20 zero-shot real-world trials.
sections.unique_caveat: The real-world evidence is 20 trials across four manipulation tasks, and the authors note that dexterous manipulation, locomotion, and tactile perception need capabilities beyond those tested.
sections.evidence: Collector score 16.149; Hugging Face paper card recorded 106 upvotes and 70 GitHub stars.

sections.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
sections.abstract: This work benchmarks rigging and instruction-driven motion across six 3D morphologies, then proposes an agent-written parametric program with deterministic execution for rigging and motion control.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce DivDynBench and an Agentic Motion Framework, arguing that compact parameterized controls paired with deterministic execution improve rigging reliability and motion accuracy.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes comparative analyses but gives no numerical benchmark results, so the magnitude of the reported improvements cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
sections.evidence: Collector score 16.059; Hugging Face paper card recorded 62 upvotes and 1,422 GitHub stars.

sections.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
sections.abstract: Real2SimLab unifies evaluation of methods that generate simulation programs from real-world observations, running each program through the original benchmark scorer and supporting training-data generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report support for 47 coding agents, five non-agent methods, and six benchmarks, plus a data-and-reward pipeline that filters benchmark videos to reduce contamination.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported platform coverage is six benchmarks; its usefulness beyond those scoring pipelines remains to be established by additional benchmark integrations.
sections.evidence: Collector score 16.025; Hugging Face paper card recorded 108 upvotes and 29 GitHub stars; one cross-list.

sections.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
sections.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs rewards an agent for gathering evidence while multiple answers remain plausible and committing when the simulator’s posterior is sufficiently concentrated.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce RLVB and the Pro Worlds visual-puzzle benchmark; across three vision-language models and three benchmarks they report an average 17.1% improvement over the base models.
sections.unique_caveat: RLVB relies on an exact answer posterior supplied by its simulator during training; the abstract reports three models and three benchmarks, so broader settings remain untested here.
sections.evidence: Collector score 15.482; Hugging Face paper card recorded 99 upvotes, 10 comments, and 27 GitHub stars.

sections.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
sections.abstract: Sage-Med-Preview is a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B active parameters, trained with curated medical data and a staged curriculum; the authors report results across 238 clinical tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a staged data-and-training recipe and report an average 58.26% on 31 public multimodal benchmarks, alongside comparisons with other open and proprietary models.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly note continuing difficulty with complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows; the evaluation also includes private benchmarks, limiting independent reproduction of that portion.
sections.evidence: Collector score 15.338; Hugging Face paper card recorded 89 upvotes and 23 GitHub stars; one cross-list.

sections.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
sections.abstract: Loom Attention lets Transformer heads attend both across tokens and over earlier heads, creating a dual-stream architecture that the authors evaluate for language modeling and downstream tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce LoomFormer’s per-token matrix memory and report that selected models match or surpass larger-compute Transformer and residual-stream baselines under their specified training budgets.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline comparisons are tied to the reported model sizes, token budgets, and language/downstream task suite; wider architecture families and workloads are not established by this abstract.
sections.evidence: Collector score 15.152; Hugging Face paper card recorded 93 upvotes and 20 GitHub stars; v2 revised inside the weekly window.

sections.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
sections.abstract: MoLT reuses key-value memories across Transformer loops, with variants designed for expressivity, efficient decoding, and skipping unused decoder traversals.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 400B-token pretraining results for U-MoLT, including improved token efficiency at 700M parameters and comparable latency to a non-looped model in their small-model inference test.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are reported for specific sizes and training regimes (up to a 3B MoE model); the abstract does not establish whether the efficiency gains persist at substantially larger scales.
sections.evidence: Collector score 15.119; Hugging Face paper card recorded 69 upvotes, two comments, and 69 GitHub stars; one cross-list. Daily rollup also featured it on 2026-11-26 at rank 2.

sections.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
sections.abstract: NightWatch pairs a computer-use agent with a lightweight streaming perception model to keep its view of a changing desktop or web interface current while the agent reasons.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that NightWatch reduces non-reasoning time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while maintaining task success, and raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with a large VLM agent.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluations cover desktop and dynamic web tasks; performance on mobile interfaces or other real-time environments is not established in the abstract.
sections.evidence: Collector score 14.988; Hugging Face paper card recorded 103 upvotes and four GitHub stars; one cross-list.
